title: Time-of-flight separation falls as 1/p²
caption: Over L = 3.7 m a kaon and a pion of the same momentum arrive Δt ≈ L(m_K² − m_π²)/(2cp²) apart: 1.39 ns at p = 1 GeV, but only 0.15 ns at 3 GeV. The exact relativistic difference (dashed) is smaller at low p, where the approximation p ≫ m fails, but follows the same 1/p² fall. TOF is a low-momentum technique.
alt: Pion–kaon flight time difference in nanoseconds against momentum from 0.5 to 3 GeV, falling steeply; the approximate curve lies above the exact dashed curve at low momentum, with 1.39 ns marked at 1 GeV.
description: β = L/(ct); for the same p the lighter particle is faster.
Approximate: Δt = 3.7 × 0.225/(2 × 3 × 10⁸ × p²) with m_K² − m_π² = 0.244 − 0.019 = 0.225 GeV².
p = 1 GeV: 1.39 ns. With 80 ps resolution this is about 17σ.
p = 3 GeV: 0.15 ns, nine times smaller.
